note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute inability to move left arm noted on waking this morning (~1 hour prior to call).
- Onset/duration/progression: Sudden onset on awakening; ongoing at time of call (~1 hour duration).
- Associated symptoms: Left-sided facial tingling since onset; slowed/harder speech; difficulty swallowing. No pain, no hand discoloration, hand not cold. No weakness of left leg. No prior similar episodes.
- Context/triggers: No unusual sleeping position or trauma reported. Lives alone.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Hypertension.
- Medications: Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented; losartan — dose/route/frequency not documented; amlodipine — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Penicillin.
- Family history: Father with heart disease.
- Social history: Ex-smoker; drinks beer (a few at weekends, a couple during the week).
- Prior hospitalizations: Not reported.

Physical Examination:
- Examination modality: Telephone consult — no clinician-performed physical exam.
- Reported/observed findings (patient-reported):
  - Left arm: unable to move (patient-reported plegia).
  - Face: tingling on left side; no reported facial asymmetry or obvious droop.
  - Speech: slower/more effortful.
  - Swallowing: some difficulty.
  - Limb perfusion: no discoloration, hand not cold.
  - Mental status: alert and able to converse.
- Vital signs: Not recorded.

Impression:
- One-line clinical impression: Suspected acute stroke presenting with acute left arm paralysis, left facial sensory change, dysarthria, and dysphagia.
- DDx (consistent with transcript):
  - Acute ischemic stroke (right hemispheric — high likelihood): Sudden focal neurological deficits on waking in a patient with hypertension and diabetes — best explains motor, facial sensory, and bulbar symptoms.
  - Intracerebral hemorrhage (right-sided — medium likelihood): Hypertension is a risk factor and hemorrhage can present similarly; differentiation requires imaging.
  - Focal seizure with post-ictal (Todd's) paresis (lower likelihood): Possible but less likely given vascular risk factors and absence of witnessed seizure; included in DDx.

Management Plan:
- Immediate actions taken:
  - Clinician arranged ambulance; ambulance dispatched and en route to patient's home.
  - Patient instructed to leave front door unlocked and to sit in the hallway by the front door for ambulance access.
  - Clinician remained on the line until ambulance arrival.
- Planned hospital actions (communicated to patient):
  - Ambulance will transport to local A&E; stroke team will assess for potential acute treatments.
- Safety/allergy note: Penicillin allergy documented — communicate to ED.
- No other medications or home treatments were advised during the call.

Patient Summary:
- Patient (DOB 12 Aug 1958) woke ~1 hour ago with sudden inability to move left arm, associated left facial tingling, slowed speech, and difficulty swallowing. GP identified concern for stroke, arranged emergency ambulance transport to A&E, and instructed patient to wait by an unlocked front door for transfer. Stroke team assessment and acute management will occur in hospital.

Key Takeaways:
- Emergency ambulance has been called and is on the way.
- Go to the front door/hallway and keep the door unlocked for ambulance access.
- ED/stroke team will assess for urgent treatment options on arrival.

Next Steps:
- Ambulance transport to emergency department now.
- Urgent hospital stroke assessment (stroke team) and investigations/treatment as indicated by ED (imaging and acute therapies to be determined by hospital clinicians).
- Communicate allergy (penicillin) and home medications to ED staff on arrival.
- GP follow-up as appropriate after hospital evaluation (not scheduled during call).

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: objective vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation), capillary blood glucose, focused neurological examination (cranial nerve exam, limb power/coordination, NIHSS), exact clock time of symptom onset / last known well, medication doses/routes/frequencies.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.
- Transcript quality comment: Telephone encounter — overall audible and coherent; occasional brief pauses and minor inaudible words but sufficient information to identify an acute focal neurological event.
